judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's two findings hold. I recomputed all ten items straight from worksheet.tex: 5+2=7, 5+4=9, 10+2=12, 4+5=9, 3+3+2=8, (5+3)=8 vs (4+2)=6 so '>', 7+6=13, 8+8=16, 4+3+2=9, and (10+4)=14 vs (10+6)=16 so '<' -- every one agrees with verify.json and with the boxed answers in the key, and the three study-guide try-its (6, 11, '<') check out too. The four-page/small-type observation is also fair for a K-1 sheet. What the judge did not check is the answer key's own Quick Answers bank: entries 6 and 10 print an em-dash, not '>' and '<'. Those are the two verified relations, so the claim that 'every answer-key result was independently recomputed and agree' is true of the worked solutions but not of the at-a-glance grading column, where 20% of the sheet is blank. ACCEPT is still the right verdict.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is the best-designed item on the sheet: both jars sit on an identical full ten-frame, so the comparison cannot be settled by which picture looks bigger -- only the 4 versus 6 loose marbles decide it. The key names why ('a useful preview of comparing teen numbers by their ones digit'), which is exactly the bridge from cardinality to place value.

The four declared traps name a counting behaviour rather than an arithmetic slip: 8 on problem 1 means a star was touched twice, 8 on problem 2 means the set-apart counter was skipped, 5 on problem 4 means only the larger group was counted, 7 on problem 9 means the third basket was never reached. A grader reading those diagnoses learns which counting principle has not landed.
Problem 2 deliberately scatters the counters in two loose bands and tells the child to cross each one off, which is the one-to-one correspondence principle being exercised rather than described.

root_causes.description: scripts/render_quick_answers.py cannot render a relation. _fmt() routes every string 'expected' through sympy.sympify(); sympify('>') raises SympifyError, and the except branch returns '---', the same token the module reserves for manual-only ids. Any compare entry with order 'relation' therefore vanishes from the bank.
evidence: verify.json id 6 expected '>', id 10 expected '<' -- both machine-verified

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified > / < relation
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, _fmt() sends every string 'expected' through sympy.sympify(); '>' and '<' raise SympifyError and fall through to the '---' branch, which the module's own docstring reserves for 'see solution' / manual-only ids. Add a relation branch before the sympify attempt: map the bare relation tokens ('>', '<', '>=', '<=', '=', '≥', '≤') to their math-mode LaTeX ($>$, $<$, $\ge$, $\le$, $=$) and return that. Everything else keeps its current behaviour, so genuinely manual ids still print '---' and remain distinguishable from a verified relation.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON containing {"id": 1, "type": "compare", "values": ["5+3", "4+2"], "order": "relation", "expected": ">"} alongside a {"id": 2, "type": "manual"} entry, and asserts the bank line for id 1 contains '$>$' while the line for id 2 is '---'. It fails today because both render '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Every worksheet whose verification_targets include 'compare' with order 'relation' regains real entries in the grader's at-a-glance bank. In this shard alone that is curr-002 (2 of 10 entries), curr-006 (2 of 8), curr-032 (2 of 10), curr-038 (part of entry 8) and curr-050 (2 of 10).
improvements.risk: Low and contained to the bank. The entries are plain text by design and are never read by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem binding gate cannot be affected. Only risk is choosing a LaTeX spelling that does not compile, which the existing compile-ak gate would catch immediately.

case_summary: A genuinely strong K-1 counting sheet: ten distinct set arrangements (neat ten-frame, scattered band, ten-frame plus loose dots, two locations, uneven rows, two-set comparison, two colours, full tray, three baskets, two jars), a clean 1-4 difficulty ramp, no repeated skeleton, and an answer key whose steps are counting narration rather than arithmetic. All ten answers, the four traps and all six study-guide results recompute correctly. The one defect I found is in the generated Quick Answers bank, which blanks the two relation answers (problems 6 and 10). Two cosmetic notes not worth an improvement entry: verify.json's internal note for problem 8 says 'Egg carton' while the worksheet and key say 'muffin tray', and a 16-cup muffin tray is an odd object; and four pages is generous for ten K-1 counting items.
